ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities

ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

rd.first: Reader says 🟡 Difficult to anticipate impact on growth; company still evaluating (+14 more under Show more)
summary: MRF's quarterly profit fell: net profit was Rs 386.99 crore versus Rs 527.43 crore a year earlier.
Total income rose to Rs 8791.58 crore from Rs 7489.00 crore, with management citing strong double-digit sales growth.
Higher raw material prices hurt profitability; price increases and cost cuts helped offset part of it.
Management expects commodity disruption and elevated raw material and logistics costs to continue.
An interim dividend of Rs 3 per share (30%) was declared; volume, margin, capacity and debt details are not given here.

top.t: Difficult to anticipate impact on growth; company still evaluating
Management expects raw material and logistics costs to remain elevated.
The impact of higher costs on margins is expected to continue

signals.t: Profit fell sharply year on year despite higher sales; raw material costs rose steeply.
higher input costs impacted profitability during the quarter
Raw Material prices continue to remain firm due to the ongoing conflict
Middle East conflict causing uncontrolled raw material cost increases and supply disruption
Sub-normal monsoon forecast may adversely impact demand
Exceptional item of Rs 77 crore charged on account of the new Labour Code.
Export turnover consolidated; second half growth constrained by geopolitical headwinds.
Key audit matter on sales-related provisions and litigation involves significant management judgement.
Past service cost from labour code changes is a key audit matter for employee benefits.
Excise/customs demand fell from 594.43 to 64.08 crore on favourable orders
Dec-25 to Mar-26: management went from saying tyre demand should stay strong to warning that the Middle East conflict is raising raw material costs and that the growth impact is hard to anticipate.
Mar-26 to Jun-26: the cost concern moved from a warning about future price hikes to a reported hit on profit, with net profit slightly lower despite higher sales.

rd.auditor: Auditor (FY2025-26): opinion unmodified; emphasis of matter: none; key audit matters: 4; contingent liabilities: not disclosed.

story.what_it_does: MRF makes and sells tyres, and its sales crossed ₹30,000 crore in FY2025-26. The notes also show some exports and raw material purchases from a related party, MRF SG PTE LTD.
story.plans: The notes give no capex or capacity plans. Management's stated plans are further price hikes and cost cuts to offset higher raw material costs, plus new product launches. A dividend was proposed for the year, and an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share was declared for FY2027.
story.moat: The notes do not describe market share, brand strength or other competitive advantages. Sales growth of about 11% in FY2025-26, and double-digit sales growth in the latest quarter, suggest demand for its products held up. Price hikes only partly offset costs, which suggests limited ability to pass on cost increases fully.

scenarios.story: Raw material pressures ease and past price hikes catch up with costs, letting profit recover alongside strong double-digit sales growth. Demand stays good, as management has said.
signals_to_watch: Raw material prices stop rising and the conflict-related disruption eases
Net profit moves back above year-ago levels (Rs 527.43 crore in the Sep-25 quarter)

scenarios.story: Sales keep growing but higher input and logistics costs keep trimming profit, as management expects. Price hikes and cost cuts offset only part of the pressure.
signals_to_watch: Management repeats that raw material and logistics costs will stay elevated
Total income keeps rising while profit before tax stays near or below year-ago levels

scenarios.story: Costs rise further and price hikes cannot keep up, so profit falls sharply as it did in the Sep-26 quarter. A sub-normal monsoon or the geopolitical headwinds could also weaken demand.
signals_to_watch: Net profit falls further below Rs 386.99 crore
Weaker demand from a sub-normal monsoon or geopolitical headwinds
